newsitem.title: INDIA: India to hold by-elections in 3 seats on May 29.
newsitem.headline: India to hold by-elections in 3 seats on May 29.

text.p: India will hold by-elections on May 29 to fill three vacancies in the lower house of parliament, the Lok Sabha, officials said on Friday.
The independent Election Commission will also hold by-elections for eight local assembly seats spread over seven states on that day, the officials said.
India's lower house has 545 seats, of which 543 members are elected and two nominated by the President.
The country's current parliament formed by April/May 1996 general elections is fragmented. It has given rise to three coalition governments in less than one year.
The vacant Lok Sabha seats include Ernakulam in the southern state of Kerala, Aska in the eastern state of Orissa and East Delhi, one of the seven seats in the Indian capital.
The vacancies in Ernakulam and Aska were created by the deaths of sitting members, while the East Delhi lawmaker resigned earlier this year.
